In handlePrepareReply the running maximum is seeded from the record's old vbal and immediately raised to the newly made ballot by the recovering replica's own entry (startRecoveryForInstance assigns inst.vbal = lastTriedBallot before building that reply), so every reply that holds a value at an older vbal - including an accept-only acceptor's command-less record at the accepted vbal - fails the element.VBallot >= lb.ballot test and is skipped. The command-less accept-only reply therefore cannot be preferred over an equal-vbal reply that carries the value, and the outcome shape is instead produced by the sibling mechanism already confirmed for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector: the recovery ignores all older-vbal replies and can commit a vector that no other replica holds. question.question: handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal for instance (Replica, Instance) and never writes inst.Status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept holds accepted attributes with Status NONE, and one that did see it keeps PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ. Does any decision depend on an accepted record carrying status ACCEPTED: can a later PreAccept for the same instance overwrite the accepted attributes because handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard cannot fire, and can a recovery that should re-accept an already accepted value instead take the phase-1 restart path because handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 needs a reply whose Status is ACCEPTED?
question.importance: An acceptor that stores accepted attributes without recording that it accepted them can (a) have those attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept at the same or a higher ballot instead of being preserved, and (b) hide from a recovering leader the fact that the value reached the accept phase, which is the distinction between re-proposing the accepted value and starting a fresh phase 1. Either effect can change the value a majority eventually commits for the instance, which is agreement-relevant rather than cosmetic; the accept phase is also the only place where a value is fixed without commands being stored, so a wrong reconstruction can also drop a command that only some replicas hold.
